46.0.s.en: 1. In praise of Joshua the son of Nun

46.0.0.en: 1 Joshua the son of Nun was valiant in the wars, the successor of Moses in the prophecies. 2 And he was, according to his name, great for the salvation of His elect, severe in vengeance on the enemies who withstood him, that he might give Israel an inheritance. 3 How great was his glory when he lifted up his hands and directed his spear against the cities! 4 Who stood before him like him in times past? For the Lord Himself delivered the enemies to him. 5 Did not the sun go back by his hand, and one day became as two? 6 He called upon the Most High, the Mighty One, when he was routing the enemies on every side, and the great Lord answered him with hailstones of mighty weight. 7 He made an assault on the nation in battle, and in the descent he destroyed those who withstood him, 8 that the nations might know all their armor, and that his war was before the Lord. Joshua was appointed as the successor of Moses in prophecy and in the leadership of the people (Deut 34:9-10), and Moses had earlier entrusted many works to him, regarding him as the faithful servant (Ex 17:9; 24:13), and before his departure he appointed him formally, before Eleazar the priest and the people, as his successor (Num 27:18-23; Deut 1:38), and after the death of Moses he prepared the children of Israel well for crossing the Jordan, and victory was achieved for him, and the inheritance of the nations (Josh 11:23).

46.0.1.en: Joshua the son of Nun was valiant in the wars, the successor of Moses in the prophecies, and according to his name he was great for the salvation of the elect, and for punishing the enemies who rose up against them, and for giving Israel its inheritance [1].

46.0.2.en: Ben Sira speaks of the commander-in-chief of the warriors, whom he called "valiant in the wars" [1]. The talk here is about the warriors, especially Joshua the son of Nun, Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and the judges, because Ben Sira was a contemporary of a priestly family that became a family of warriors, namely the Maccabees. These zealous priests drew the people to resist the occupier who insisted on defiling the Temple of the Lord, breaking the divine commandments, and accepting the worship of idols.

46.0.3.en: Ben Sira presented the work of God in the life of Joshua, who fought so that Israel might possess the Promised Land [1-6]. By this he supports his contemporaries in resisting the successors of Alexander the Great and working for the holiness of the house of the Lord and the Promised Land.

46.0.4.en: "Joshua was, according to his name, great for the salvation of the elect [1]," for its meaning is "the Lord saves." He led the people and defeated the Canaanites, beginning with the city of Jericho (Josh 6). He was a type of the awaited Messiah, our Savior, who was called Jesus.

46.1.0.en: "The battles of the Lord": the heroism of Joshua was achieved by his hiding in the true Commander, the Lord Himself; therefore the battles of Joshua were called "the battles of the Lord" [3]. So also, to the extent that we hide in the Lord, believing in our spiritual striving that the two sides of the battle are the Lord Himself and the devil, our victory is achieved by our hiding in Him, and we are counted "soldiers of Christ" (2 Tim 2:3).

46.2.0.en: The Lord moved nature to serve Joshua and his people (Josh 10:12-14), and He prolonged the day of the battle and made it as long as two days [4]. So also, when the Lord leads our battle against the devil, He grants us what seems impossible, since He directs everything for the sake of our victory. But the secret of Joshua's victory is that he did not fight with the sword only, but with prayer also, for he "called upon the Most High, the Mighty One" [5], "and the great Lord answered him."

46.2.1.en: He speaks here of Joshua's victory over Amalek (Ex 17:8-13). Moses needed Aaron and Hur to hold up his outstretched hands until the battle was ended, while Joshua continued to fight Amalek to the end.

46.2.2.en: v I pass on to Joshua the son of Nun, a type of the Lord both in name (Jesus) and in work, who crossed over into the Jordan, and subdued the hostile kingdoms, and divided the land among the victorious people; he who dealt with every city and village and mountain and river and hill and border, and imparted to him the kingdoms of the heavenly Jerusalem, that is, those that belong to the Church [1].

46.2.3.en: St. Jerome: How great was his glory when he lifted up his hands and stretched out his sword as a warning to the cities! [2]

46.2.4.en: His weapon was "lifting up his hands in prayer," and he had authority, so the sun did not go back, that is, it did not set until the victory was completed, for the day became as long as two days [4]. The lifting up of the hand here means declaring war on the enemies.

46.2.5.en: Who before him stood firm like him? For he is the one who led the wars of the Lord [3].

46.2.6.en: Joshua did not enter into a battle of his own; he did not defend himself, nor his dignity, nor seek any spoil, but hid in the Lord to lead "the battles of the Lord."

46.2.7.en: Did not the sun go back at a sign from his hand, and one day became as two? [4]

46.2.8.en: It is recorded in the history of Herodotus that the priests showed him documents indicating the existence of a day longer than usual; likewise in China they affirm that there was a long day in the reign of the Emperor "Yu," who was a contemporary of Joshua the son of Nun; and in Mexico there are documents indicating that a long day occurred in history in the same year in which Joshua was continuing his victories [2].

46.2.9.en: He called upon the Most High, the Mighty One, when the enemies were pressing him on every side.

46.3.0.en: And the great Lord answered him with hailstones of mighty weight [5].

46.4.0.en: He crushed those nations in the war, and on the slope of Beth-horon he destroyed those who withstood him, that the nations might know his complete armor, for he was fighting the war of the Lord [6].

46.4.1.en: Joshua went up to war against five kings, and the Lord Himself strengthened him, saying to him: "Fear them not: for I have delivered them into thine hand; there shall not a man of them stand before thee" (Josh 10:8). He came upon them suddenly, going up all night, and the Lord Himself discomfited the enemy and slew them with a great slaughter at Gibeon, and chased them along the way that goeth up to Beth-horon, and smote them to Azekah, and unto Makkedah... And as the enemy fled from before Israel, while they were on the descent of Beth-horon, the Lord cast down great hailstones from heaven upon them, and they were more which died with hailstones than they whom the children of Israel slew with the sword. It is as though the victory over these kings was achieved by two things: the sword and the hailstones coming down from heaven.

46.4.2.en: v Joshua the son of Nun, the righteous, who became a perfect disciple of the great Teacher (Moses), was also beautiful.

46.4.3.en: He also wished that the love of life might triumph in him, and that he might draw near to God in perfection.

46.4.4.en: He kept purity while serving in the tabernacle of time (the tent of meeting), and became for the people a second Moses before God.

46.4.5.en: He fought to establish the word of the Lord among the peoples, and the mighty works he wrought made known how exalted his beauty was [3].

46.5.s.en: 2. In praise of Joshua and Caleb the son of Jephunneh

46.5.0.en: 8 For he followed the Mighty One. 9 And in the days of Moses he did a work of mercy, he and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, in that they stood against the enemy, and turned away the people from sin, and stilled the wicked murmuring. 10 And they alone were preserved of the six hundred thousand footmen, to bring them into the inheritance, into a land that floweth with milk and honey. 11 And the Lord gave strength unto Caleb, and it remained with him unto his old age; so that he went up to the high place of the land, which his seed obtained for an inheritance, 12 that all the children of Israel might see that it is good to follow the Lord.

46.5.1.en: And in truth he followed the Lord. Even in the days of Moses he showed his faithfulness, he and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, for they stood firm before the congregation, to keep the people from sin and to stop their wicked murmuring [7].

46.5.2.en: Sirach added to Joshua his famous companion Caleb the son of Jephunneh, recalling that the two urged Israel to victory over the holy land in the days of Moses [7-8]. In the days of Ben Sira there were many leaders who were turning away from divine wisdom and the commandment and were clinging to Hellenistic thought. Therefore Sirach presented these two men, whom the people resisted in the days of Moses, who persevered in spreading the spirit of faith and trust in the divine promises.

46.5.3.en: v When a man finds himself in a state that does not agree with his will and inclinations, he sees himself as in prison and torment. Therefore you must be content with what you have, so that you may not suffer (from your circumstances) and become ungrateful (and murmuring), and so wrong yourself without knowing it. But there is one way: despise temporal gifts [4].

46.5.4.en: St. Anthony the Great v Question: What if he obeys, but murmurs while he works?

46.5.5.en: Answer: The Apostle says: "Do all things without murmurings and disputings" (Phil 2:14). The murmurer turns aside from the unity of the brethren, and perhaps they will not use his work. For it is clear that such a one is afflicted with lack of faith and unsteadiness in hope [5].

46.5.6.en: St. Basil the Great And in truth they alone were preserved of the six hundred thousand footmen of the people, to enter into the inheritance, into a land flowing with milk and honey [8].

46.5.7.en: When Joshua and Caleb the son of Jephunneh gave their reports about the Promised Land, its good things, and its inhabitants, there was murmuring among the people and weeping, longing to return again to slavery under a new leader other than the prophet Moses. Therefore none of that generation entered the Promised Land except Joshua and Caleb.

46.5.8.en: And the Lord gave strength to Caleb, which remained with him until his old age, for he went up to the heights of the land which his seed kept as an inheritance [9].

46.5.9.en: Caleb gained great fame for his steadfastness in the commandment of the Lord while the majority opposed him. Caleb came to Joshua and said to him: "Behold, the Lord hath kept me alive, as he said, these forty and five years, even since the Lord spake this word unto Moses, while the children of Israel wandered in the wilderness: and now, lo, I am this day fourscore and five years old. As yet I am as strong this day as I was in the day that Moses sent me: as my strength was then, even so is my strength now, for war, both to go out, and to come in. Now therefore give me this mountain, whereof the Lord spake in that day; for thou heardest in that day how the Anakims were there, and that the cities were great and fenced: if so be the Lord will be with me, then I shall be able to drive them out, as the Lord said" (Josh 14:10-12).

46.6.0.en: That all the children of Israel might see the goodness of following the Lord [10].

46.6.1.en: God raised Caleb and Joshua above the congregation in their generation, which revealed their following of the Lord (46:10).

46.7.0.en: 13 And the judges, every one by his name, whose heart went not a whoring, nor departed from the Lord. 14 Let their memorial be blessed, and let their bones flourish out of their place. 15 And let their name be renewed, and let their sons glorify them.

46.7.1.en: And the judges also, each by his name, whose hearts did not fall into idolatry, and none of them departed from the Lord: may their memory be blessed! [11]

46.7.2.en: Sirach linked the judges with Joshua and Caleb without pointing to any of them by name. If Ben Sira began with Enoch up to Moses and Aaron as heroes of faith who entered into covenants with God and practiced worship to Him with sincerity, he now moves to heroes in military battles whose aim was to destroy the worship of idols, to worship God alone, and to establish a house for the Lord in which worship would be practiced through the generations. He then moves on to the prophet Samuel, at whose hands Saul and David the kings were anointed, one according to the desire of the people, and the other according to the mind of God [13].

46.7.3.en: And may their bones live again from their graves [6], and may the name of those honored live on in their sons! [12]

46.7.4.en: The words of the prophet Ezekiel about the resurrection of the dead (Ezek 37:1-14) were in his mind as he declared his faith in the resurrection from the dead. With burning zeal Ben Sira prays for his disciples and the whole new generation, that they may walk in the way of their fathers, the heroes of faith.

46.7.5.en: In his praise of the forefathers he gave a testimony to belief in the resurrection. "May their bones flourish" (46:12; 49:10). The flourishing of a plant signifies life. It is as though the dry bones enjoy the resurrection and life flourishes.

46.7.6.en: He also spoke of the prophet Elijah, whose return is expected to reform Israel (48:10). Solomon, who began his life with a spirit of godliness and wisdom, fell because of his bodily lusts. It is a lesson for believers, that no one should rely on being a member of the Church, nor on the holiness of his fathers, nor on the holiness he attained in his youth (Sir 49:4-5).

46.7.7.en: v Gideon was watchful, and Barak was full of faith, and Samson was a Nazirite, and Samuel was enlightened by prophecy [7].

46.8.s.en: 4. In praise of the prophet Samuel

46.8.0.en: 16 Samuel, beloved of the Lord, a prophet of the Lord, established the kingdom, and anointed rulers over his people. 17 By the law of the Lord he judged the congregation, and the Lord looked upon Jacob. 18 By his faithfulness he was proved to be a prophet, and by his word he was known to be faithful in vision. 19 He called upon the Lord, the Mighty One, when his enemies pressed him on every side, and he offered a sucking lamb. 20 Then the Lord thundered from heaven, and with a great noise made his voice to be heard, 21 and destroyed the princes of the Tyrians, and all the lords of the Philistines. 22 And before the time of his long sleep, he made protestation before the Lord and his anointed, I have not taken any man's goods, so much as a shoe, and no man did accuse him. 23 And after his sleep he prophesied, and showed the king his end, and lifted up his voice from the earth in prophecy, to blot out the wickedness of the people.

46.8.1.en: The prophet of the Lord, Samuel, beloved of the Lord, established the kingdom and anointed rulers for his people [13].

46.8.2.en: Samuel is considered a symbol of the transition from the system of judges to the system of kings. Samuel, the last of the judges, also looked to not separating worship from the war against idols. Ben Sira took interest in the person of Samuel as the man of transition, who lived as a judge and a prophet in dark circumstances. The man of transition had to be marked by diverse aspects of leading the people and the leaders, so that he might succeed in fulfilling his mission. Samuel is one of the most beloved figures to the hearts of the Jews, for he combined in his person several qualities:

46.8.3.en: A. Prophet of the Lord, the first of God's prophets after Moses, who declared God's will and desire to the leaders as well as to the people [13].

46.8.4.en: B. Beloved of the Lord, a sign of a personal relationship with his Lord [13]. And he is faithful and trustworthy (1 Sam 9:6).

46.8.5.en: C. He kept the law of the Lord in his decisions and conduct [14].

46.8.6.en: D. He believed in the promises of the Lord to Jacob the son of Isaac the son of Abraham, "the Lord looked upon Jacob" [14].

46.8.7.en: E. He was marked by faithfulness and sincerity and the sanctification of his words, so he was known to be a true and honest prophet [15].

46.8.8.en: F. He was not like the other judges, the spiritual warriors, but was a prophet who established the school of the prophets, who taught the people the life of prayer and responding to the will of God. He was a spiritual leader who continued his work during the reign of King Saul and after the anointing of the prophet David as king.

46.8.9.en: G. He was a man of prayer [16] at the time when the people asked to have a king like all the nations, in whom they might glory. Although he opposed them, the Lord asked him to respond to their request after he warned them of what they would suffer from the king and his family and even his tribe.

46.8.10.en: He judged the congregation according to the law of the Lord, and the Lord looked upon Jacob [14].

46.8.11.en: What occupied the prophet Samuel was obedience to the divine commandment. When Saul exceeded his limits, disobeying the divine commandment by offering sacrifices that are the work of the priest and not the king, the prophet Samuel came to rebuke him, saying to him: "What hast thou done?" (1 Sam 13:11). Instead of examining himself and confessing his fault, he cast the blame on Samuel, saying: "Because I saw that the people were scattered from me, and that thou camest not within the days appointed, and that the Philistines gathered themselves together at Michmash; therefore said I, The Philistines will come down now upon me to Gilgal, and I have not made supplication unto the Lord: I forced myself therefore, and offered a burnt offering" (1 Sam 13:11-12).

46.8.12.en: By his faithfulness he proved that he was a true prophet, and by his words he was known to be a faithful seer [15].

46.8.13.en: All Israel from Dan even to Beer-sheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the Lord (1 Sam 3:20).

46.8.14.en: And so he called upon the Mighty Lord when his enemies troubled him on every side, and when he offered a little lamb [16].

46.9.0.en: Then the Lord thundered from heaven, and with a great noise made His voice to be heard [17].

46.9.1.en: It refers to the victories of the Jews over the Philistines at Mizpeh (1 Sam 7:7-11), where the Lord thundered that day upon the Philistines and troubled them, so they were terrified and were smitten before them.

46.10.0.en: And he destroyed the leaders of the people of Tyre, and all the lords of the Philistines [18].

46.10.1.en: And before the time of his everlasting sleep, he called the people to bear witness before the Lord and His anointed:

46.11.0.en: "I have not taken any man's goods, so much as a shoe," and in truth no one accused him [19].

46.11.1.en: Ben Sira sees that death is a sleep of the body, while the soul departs to God. The prophet Samuel gave a plain farewell address in which he called them to witness before God and His anointed to his faithfulness toward them and that he had not exploited them, and he reminded them of the Lord's blessings and works with them, and rebuked them for asking for a king, opening before them the door of hope in the Lord who loves His people. What the prophet Samuel did here was not a defense of himself, for no one had accused him of anything, but he intended to instruct the new king. And as St. John Chrysostom says: [No one accused him; he did not utter this to justify himself, but because he had anointed a king, and he wanted to teach him to be meek and gentle under the cover of his defense of himself... He uttered this so that (the king) might be in a better condition [8].]

46.12.0.en: And even after his sleep he prophesied and showed the king his end, and lifted up his voice from the earth in prophecy to blot out the wickedness of the people [20].

46.12.1.en: David's taking refuge with Achish put King Saul in a difficult position when the Philistines rose against Israel. But Saul, when danger came upon him and the Lord did not answer him because of his continual evils, took refuge with the woman who had a familiar spirit (1 Sam 28), although he had banned those with familiar spirits and wizards. He disguised himself, and asked her to bring up the spirit of Samuel that he might seek his counsel. The Book of Ben Sira says that God allowed him to speak with him in order to rebuke him for his evil conduct, and some think that Satan came in the form of Samuel to speak with him, because it is not possible for her to summon the spirits of the departed.

46.13.s.en: Your hands train mighty giants of strength!

46.13.0.en: v The devil thought that Your people would collapse at the death of Moses.

46.13.1.en: Your hands which trained Moses, great among the prophets, trained his disciple Joshua!

46.13.2.en: Your voice resounds through the generations: "As I was with Moses, so I will be with thee" (Josh 1:5).

46.13.3.en: Moses could not cross the Jordan, yet behold, Joshua crossed it with the leaders and the people!

46.13.4.en: At a sign from his hand the sun stood still, and the day was prolonged to two days (Josh 10:12).

46.13.5.en: He took hold of the sword to fight, but You cast hailstones upon his enemies! (Josh 10:11)

46.13.6.en: v Joshua and Caleb entered the Promised Land, apart from all those who came out of Egypt.

46.13.7.en: Caleb grew old, but his strength never declined.

46.13.8.en: At the age of eighty-five his strength was as it was at forty.

46.13.9.en: You were glorified in the old man who went up to the heights of the land like a strong youth!

46.13.10.en: v Satan stirred up the pagan peoples so that they would not cease fighting the people of God.

46.13.11.en: And on the other hand, You sent pious judges who bear witness to You.

46.13.12.en: v The house of Eli the old priest became corrupt, and his two sons brought bitterness upon the people.

46.13.13.en: You visited Your people with a little child (Samuel). What shall we call him? You appeared to him and gave him the spirit of prophecy.

46.13.14.en: You called him Your beloved, for he clung to Your law.

46.13.15.en: He destroyed the leaders of the pagans, and his heart was not occupied with gold or silver.

46.13.16.en: He asked nothing of anyone, for You are his treasure.

46.13.17.en: His soul was embittered for the heart of the wicked King Saul.

46.13.18.en: You did not ignore his tears, and You anointed the greatest of kings, the prophet David!

46.13.19.en: Your hand, O my God, has wrought wonders, and still works, and will work until the day of Your final coming.

46.13.20.en: To You be glory, O mighty Shepherd of souls!
